title: MX+: Pushing the Limits of Microscaling Formats for Efficient Large Language Model Serving
problem: The 4-bit Microscaling (MXFP4) format suffers severe accuracy degradation when applied to LLM activation tensors because activation outlier values (Block Max, BM) are encoded with only 1 mantissa bit, causing large quantization errors that also corrupt the entire 32-element block via the shared exponent scale. This makes MXFP4 impractical for production LLM inference despite its potential bandwidth and compute savings.
motivation: LLM inference is memory-bandwidth-bound, making 4-bit quantization critical for cost-effective serving, yet the current MXFP4 standard fails on activation quantization due to outliers—blocking industry adoption of the lowest-bit MX tier.
method: The core problem is that Block Max outliers in MXFP4 have only 1 mantissa bit (precision bits) for their value, causing large rounding errors that corrupt the entire 32-element block. MX+ solves this by repurposing the Block Max's exponent bits—which are always set to maximum and unused—as extra mantissa bits instead, changing the encoding from E2M1 (2 exponent bits, 1 mantissa bit) to E0M3 (3 mantissa bits) and tripling precision. To locate the Block Max within each 32-element block, an 8-bit index is added (5 bits for position, 3 bits reserved). MX+ supports both software and hardware paths: on regular GPUs it decomposes the Block Max into high and low halves (BMH, BML) and runs a standard matrix multiply plus one sparse matrix multiply; on NVIDIA Blackwell it adds dedicated hardware units (BM Detector, Forward and Swap Units, BM Compute Unit) to compute Block Max operations in parallel with the main pipeline, adding 0.020mm² at 28nm.
key_novelty: MX+ repurposes the Block Max element's exponent bits as additional mantissa (precision) bits, since the Block Max's exponent is always at maximum (a fixed property of the format), enabling outlier precision improvements without changing block structure, adding storage overhead, or requiring software modifications.
contributions: MX+ format: non-intrusive extension to MX that represents BM outliers with additional mantissa precision (e.g., E0M3 vs E2M1 for MXFP4), with only 0.25 bits/element overhead
Software integration for MX+ using existing NVIDIA Tensor Cores (CUTLASS+vLLM) achieving up to +42.15% accuracy improvement over MXFP4 with 1.13x slowdown max
Hardware Tensor Core integration (BM Detector + FSU + BCU at 28nm, 0.020mm2) achieving near-MX throughput (0.38% slowdown) with substantially higher model accuracy
Comprehensive comparative analysis of industry BFP variants (MSFP, SMX, MX) showing MX consistently outperforms alternatives at equivalent bit widths

metrics.accuracy: MXFP4+ vs MXFP4: up to +42.15% task accuracy improvement on Llama-3.1-8B; perplexity reduced from 27.69 to ~9.5 (WikiText-2) for Llama-3.1-8B
metrics.speedup: Hardware integration: 0.38% slowdown vs MXFP4; software integration A-MXFP4+: 1.13x slowdown max at long output lengths
metrics.area: 0.020mm2 at 28nm per Tensor Core for MX+ hardware (BM Detector + FSU + BCU)
metrics.other: 0.25 bits/element storage overhead; end-to-end vLLM speedup over BF16 close to MXFP4 at decode-dominant inference

limitations: MX+ evaluation is limited to post-training quantization (direct-cast inference); quantization-aware training results are only shown for smaller vision/CNN models, and the approach has not been validated on mixture-of-experts or very long-context LLMs.
primary_theme: outlier-aware extension of MX block floating-point for 4-bit LLM inference
